params.body:
`bin/fold-twins.mjs` comes back, with `--plan`.

**Why:** I removed the script as a one-off in #211. A day later it's needed again: the 59 public trends contain 10 groups of twins under the fold rule (patterns or signals overlapping by half). Twins arise whenever readings are approved in batches, so this is a recurring tool.

**`--plan plan.json`** applies an editor's decision as data: per group the trend that stays (`head`) and the ones that fold into it (`fold`). The choices are made on a choice page.
- The groups are not recomputed, so a member the editor kept apart stays apart.
- A step is only carried out while every trend in it is still live, not replaced and public.
- It is dry by default; `--apply` links. It uses the same `linkTwins` as on 2026-09-23: `superseded_by` plus `superseded_at`, the folded trend's signals go to the one that stays, and the site sends the old address there (`trend_aliases`, 301).

Also fixed: the import of `db` (`{db}`).

Checks: a plan dry run on an empty database (0 folds); the full suite, 948 tests, 0 failures.
params.title: fold-twins back, with a plan an editor made
